findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Upon arrival, there wasn't a certified food protection manager available. A CFPM arrived shortly after the start of the inspection to correct the violation. Person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the facility will work to get the main cook food manager certified. Ensure that there is always at least one employee who is food manager certified during operating hours.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were a handful of mouse dropping observed on floor of the dry storage area. Shown to the PIC and discussed routinely cleaning of storage area. Ensure that the area is cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent the accumulation of droppings.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were two containers of bread loafs stored on the floor of the indoor building. The PIC mentioned that the breads are normally stored off the floor and in a different area. Ensure that bread loafs are stored at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution present inside of the shed where food is being cold held, hot held, prepped, and served. Discussed with the PIC that a sanitizer solution shall be present to sanitize all food contact surfaces. The facility will use a sanitizer bottle for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
None of the employees working at the time of the inspection could show proof of food handler certificates. The PIC was given a reference sheet of websites so that employees can obtain food handler licenses. Ensure that all employees who aren't food manager certified obtain food handler certificates. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution available while food prep was occurring. Discussed with PIC and a sanitizer bucket was created. Demonstrated how to properly test sanitizer solutions using (CL)test strips. Ensure that there is ALWAYS a sanitizer bucket available during hours of operation (including the shack where food is being cooked and held).
